facts.text: Dayton was founded on April 1, 1796 by the Thompson Party and named after Revolutionary War captain Jonathan Dayton.
The city sits on a low floodplain where the Great Miami River meets the Stillwater and Mad rivers, a spot that helped shape its early growth.
Dayton is the birthplace of aviation pioneers Orville and Wilbur Wright, whose legacy is celebrated at the Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park.
Poet Paul Laurence Dunbar’s home in Dayton is now a state memorial museum, preserving the legacy of a nationally celebrated African‑American author.
The historic Victoria Theatre downtown hosts everything from Broadway shows to summer film series, keeping Dayton’s cultural scene lively.
Wright‑Patterson Air Force Base, once McCook Field, was the site where the 1995 Dayton Agreement was negotiated, ending the Bosnian war.
